Welcome to Knightsbridge School
We offer a vibrant and nurturing community that spans from Early Years and Juniors through to a successful Senior School. At KS, we blend academic excellence with an ecosystem of happiness and high pastoral standards.
Learn more about what makes us distinctive…
Ready to discover what makes us special?
Explore our website, download our prospectus, or book a visit on either a small group tour or an upcoming open morning, and feel the KS magic for yourself. We can’t wait to welcome you.
A Leading Independent Day School in the Heart of London
Knightsbridge School is an independent prep and senior school in central London, welcoming children from Nursery through to GCSEs. As one of the capital’s established independent day schools, we combine high academic standards with a genuinely personal, pastoral approach — because we believe every child does their best work when they feel known, supported and challenged in equal measure.
What Sets Us Apart
Families choose Knightsbridge from among London’s many independent and prep schools for a few clear reasons: small class sizes that mean no child is overlooked, a fully co-educational environment from Nursery to Senior School, and a central London location that makes school life part of the wider city rather than separate from it. Whether you’re looking for a private prep school for your youngest child or an independent senior school through to GCSEs, our staff work with families at every stage of that journey.
A Curriculum Built Around Every Child
Our curriculum spans the academic core alongside a strong offering in sport, music and the arts, supported by a wide range of co-curricular clubs and activities that run throughout the week. See our full Junior and Senior School curriculum pages for year-by-year detail.
Where would you like to go next?
Knightsbridge Highlights
Year 6, Miss Liz and Miss Sandra enjoyed a trip...
Take a look at Knightsbridge pupils getting an exclusive taste...
On Thursday 10th September, Year 1 Knightsbridge School pupils were...
On Thursday 10th September, Year 2 Knightsbridge School pupils had...
Frequently Asked Questions
Where is Knightsbridge School located?
Knightsbridge School is based at 67 Pont Street in Knightsbridge, central London.
What ages does Knightsbridge School accept?
We welcome children from our Early Years setting (age 3) through to Senior School and GCSEs (age 16).
Is Knightsbridge School co-educational?
Yes – all genders are taught together at every stage.
How do I apply to Knightsbridge School?
You can find full details of our admissions process, including how to book a tour or attend an open morning, on our Admissions pages.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos & Aims | Prep School London | Knightsbridge School
pageCache.text:
”KS fosters a strong sense of community and welcomes parental involvement. It provides a warm, supportive environment where children flourish.”
The Good Schools Guide
Our Ethos & Code
One Eco-System of Happiness
At Knightsbridge, we are proud to develop happy, confident students who are interesting and interested in the world around them. We are thrilled to provide a stimulating education and supportive pastoral care for our students from Nursery to GCSE.
In this way, students get what they need when they need it and are encouraged to carve out their own path, whether it be academic or the arts. Each will be unique. The focus on the whole child is achieved by providing opportunities across academic subjects, sport, performing and creative arts, and well-being.
Encouraging students to embrace the opportunity, find the thing or things they love, and have a go. Valuing the skills and talents each person has is at the heart of all that we do, and by creating an ecosystem of happiness, we believe this leads to all-round achievement!
Six Aims
What are our ‘Twelve Values’?
We follow a simple set of 12 rules known as the KS Code, which was written by Magoo Giles, Founder and Principal of Knightsbridge School, in memory of his own parents. ⁠
⁠The KS code is built on human values and we expect all of our children, parents, and staff to follow it both in and out of school. ⁠
Of course, no one is perfect, and mistakes are made, but the KS Code allows us to be ourselves and to push our individual strengths and weaknesses, learning to enjoy our successes, push ourselves, learn to fail well and fast, and learn from it in a community or family that really cares.
Frequently Asked Questions About The KS Code
What is the KS Code?
The KS Code is a set of values written by Magoo Giles, Founder and Principal of Knightsbridge School, in memory of his own parents. It is built on human values and is expected to be followed by children, parents and staff, both in and out of school.
What are Knightsbridge School's Six Aims?
The Six Aims are Atmosphere, Autonomy, All-rounder, Attitude, Achievement and Action, covering the learning environment, independence, all-round development, love of learning, academic potential and community responsibility.

”KS fosters a strong sense of community and welcomes parental involvement. It provides a warm, supportive environment where children flourish.”
The Good Schools Guide
Why Choose Knightsbridge School?
We are incredibly proud of our happy, vibrant, and purposeful community, built over two decades in the heart of London. Stepping through our blue doors, you are welcomed into a top-rated independent school in Knightsbridge where the “KS Magic” is palpable. You will hear the buzz of students and teachers chatting as they move between lessons, sports matches, and over 70 extra-curricular clubs.
Book a Visit View Our Prospectus
The Knightsbridge Difference
All-Through Education: A Seamless 3-16 Journey
By providing a continuous path from Nursery through to GCSEs, we eliminate the stress of transition exams (7+, 11+, and 13+) and replace it with stability, confidence, and growth.
Deeply Rooted Relationships: Our teachers don’t just know your child’s grades; they know their character. This long-term perspective allows us to tailor support and celebrate individual progress with a depth that only an all-through school can provide.
A Consistent Moral Compass: The “KS Code” is interwoven into every stage of the journey. From the first day of Nursery to the final GCSE exam, our values remain at the heart of their learning.
Mentorship in Action: Our Seniors serve as natural role models for our younger pupils, fostering a unique family atmosphere where every child, from age 3 to 16, feels they truly belong.
Academic Excellence Grounded in Happiness
As a leading academically non-selective independent school in Knightsbridge, we consistently prove that high achievement and happiness go hand-in-hand.
See our recent 11+ results as well as our GCSE results and future schools destinations here.
Brilliant Pastoral Care and Wellbeing Support
We believe that children learn best when they feel safe, happy, and a sense of belonging.
Discover what our community says about Pastoral Care at Knightsbridge.
Exceptional Enrichment and Sport
We leverage our central London location to provide a vibrant backdrop for discovery beyond the classroom
Learn more about the facilities we use.
A Close-Knit, Inclusive Community
KS is the “beating heart” of the community, where families from all over the world join a supportive and inclusive network.
Learn more about Charitable engagement, Sustainability, and our Parent’s Association.
An All Round Education - the Arts at KS
An “All-Rounder” Ethos: We believe every child should “give it a go,” fostering self-expression and confidence through specialist-led lessons in Music, Drama, Dance, and Visual Arts.
Professional Performance & Exhibition: From our Show Choir performing at The Berkeley to Drama productions at The Chelsea Theatre, our pupils showcase their talents in professional settings across London.
Accredited Excellence: We provide a clear pathway for talent through prestigious external qualifications, including LAMDA, Trinity Drama, and ABRSM.
Learn more about Performing Arts in our Junior and Senior School.
Experience the ‘KS Magic’ in Person
The best way to understand why we are a top-choice independent school in Knightsbridge is to see us in action. We invite families to step through our blue doors and discover the vibrant community that makes Knightsbridge School so special.
Guided Tours: Our one-hour tours offer a firsthand look at a normal school day.
Open Mornings: Join us at one of our upcoming open mornings or stay & plays, the perfect opportunity to come along and learn more about life at Knightsbridge School.
Convenient Location: Visit us at 67 Pont Street, just a short walk from Knightsbridge and Sloane Square stations.

Headmaster & Founder’s Welcome
Welcome from Mr Adam Anstey, Headmaster
A warm welcome to Knightsbridge School, a leading all-through school in the heart of London.
At Knightsbridge, we are passionate about providing an innovative, forward-thinking education, focused on giving students the very best start in life. Our approach combines research-backed methods, best practice and an unwavering dedication to each student. We believe in building strong foundations that will empower young people to thrive and make meaningful contributions to the world.
That starts with knowing every student exceptionally well.
Every journey is different. Some students need greater challenge, others additional support, encouragement or simply the right opportunity at the right moment. Whatever they need, we are with them, and you, every step of the way. This highly personalised approach, built around close relationships between students, families and school, is central to the Knightsbridge experience.
We are ambitious for everyone and believe that every student is capable of achieving highly. Academic excellence matters, but education should never be defined by results alone. We want our students to become curious, confident and adaptable young people who are comfortable asking questions, taking considered risks and learning from mistakes.
Our approach is grounded in research, but also in the belief that great schools are built through continual improvement. We look for the marginal gains: the small, thoughtful improvements, informed by feedback and reflection, that collectively can make an extraordinary difference to a student over time.
Knightsbridge is built on strong foundations. Our responsibility is to preserve what makes the school distinctive while remaining curious about what we can make even better.
As an internationally diverse school in the heart of London, we have an extraordinary opportunity to develop a genuinely global outlook. Our students grow up alongside different cultures, perspectives and experiences. We want them to understand the world around them, while also recognising the important role they can play within it.
That means developing creativity, leadership, resilience and an entrepreneurial mindset. Not because every student will become an entrepreneur, but because every young person should have the confidence to spot opportunities, solve problems, turn ideas into action and become a catalyst for positive change.
The KS Code provides an important compass throughout this journey. How we treat others, how we respond to challenge and how we contribute to our community matter just as much as what we achieve. Character and ambition should strengthen one another.
Ultimately, our aim is for every student to leave Knightsbridge with strong foundations, a clear sense of who they are and the confidence to pursue their own path. We want them equipped to lead extraordinary lives, while understanding that a truly successful life is also measured by the difference we make to others, our communities and the wider world.
I very much look forward to welcoming you to Knightsbridge School.
Adam Anstey Headmaster

Early Years Curriculum
At Knightsbridge School, our Early Years provision is built upon the Statutory Framework for the EYFS (2024). We believe that a child’s first steps in education should be filled with wonder, providing a secure foundation that inspires a lifelong love of learning.
Using the Birth to 5 Matters guidance, we focus on nurturing the whole child. Our curriculum is designed around the seven areas of learning, starting with the three Prime Areas that underpin all future development:
As children grow in confidence, these areas support their progress in the four Specific Areas: Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World, and Expressive Arts and Design.
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Personal, Social, and Emotional Development
Learning Through Discovery
We champion an open-ended, play-based approach where teachers act as expert facilitators. By following each child’s unique interests and pace, we foster the Characteristics of Effective Learning, ensuring pupils become resilient, creative, and critical thinkers. These early experiences do more than just teach—they build the social fluency and cognitive skills that benefit children throughout their entire school career.
A World Beyond the Classroom
Education at Knightsbridge School extends well beyond the classroom walls. Our Reception pupils enjoy a rich variety of specialist-led sessions and outdoor adventures, including:
Literacy
Literacy
We instil a love of Literacy from the start of the Foundation Stage. Each classroom has a welcoming and inviting Literacy and reading area and children develop reading and writing skills through adult-led and child-initiated activities. Story time features as an important part of the day, where children enjoy listening to and discussing stories. We use the Read, Write, Inc. scheme to teach children phonics. The children begin learning letter sounds in the Nursery class and the scheme works progressively and systematically throughout Reception, where the children learn to independently read and write using Ditty Books. Children at Knightsbridge School are encouraged to ‘write for a purpose.’ This then means for example children will write letters, lists, postcards, Christmas cards, labels or recounts.
Maths
Maths
Children acquire skills in numbers and space, shape and measure through a range of practical, hands-on activities. Mathematics in the Early Years is also split into Number and Numerical Patterns. Each Foundation Stage classroom has Maths activities throughout the space, where the children explore mathematical concepts and develop their understanding. Maths is taught daily in whole class and small group sessions as well as being an intrinsic part of independent learning during self-selective activities (Continuous Provision).
Self-selective activities (continuous provision)
Self-selective activities (continuous provision)
Continuous provision forms the most part of a Foundation Stage timetable. Children learn through topics that change half-termly and the whole EYFS curriculum is represented in these sessions. Children independently choose activities that are carefully planned and set up in the relevant areas of the classroom. Adults also direct the learning and teaching every day by adapting plans to facilitate the children’s interests. Children become independent and enthusiastic learners who push their own learning forward. They acquire and consolidate skills and knowledge through inquiry, investigation, exploration and perseverance.
Languages
Languages
All children in the Foundation Stage learn a second language. Children can learn either French or Spanish and they have two 30 minute lessons a week.
Physical Development
Physical Development
Physical development is an important part of the EYFS curriculum and is an area we focus on at KS before other skills develop. For example, before letter formation progresses we need the children to gain muscle strength in their fingers, hands and arms. We make use of all the available outdoor space in close proximity to the school. Children enjoy Forest School sessions at Holland Park, where they explore nature and learn about forest animals and their habitats. We use St Luke’s park and the Holland Park Adventure Playground as a free play playground, enabling the children to climb, swing, jump, run and balance on all the apparatus.
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive Arts and Design are split into ‘creating with materials’ and ‘being imaginative and expressive.’ Children learn to safely use and explore a variety of materials, tools, and equipment where they then share their creations explaining the process they have used. They are encouraged to communicate this to not only their class teachers but also their peers. The Early Years team work alongside the Creative Arts team at KS to support children to express themselves through Dance, Drama, and Music.
Performing Arts
Performing Arts
Our KS code tells us to ‘do something creative every day’. Music, Drama and Dance lessons are a highlight of the Foundation stage timetable and are taught by highly-skilled specialist teachers. The Nursery and Reception classes perform a Christmas Play (Twas the Night Before Christmas and Santa is on Strike) every year, as well as taking part in Harvest Festival, a Summer Show, and class assemblies.

Enrichment & Extracurriculars
At Knightsbridge School, we believe education is most powerful when it moves beyond the four walls of a classroom. We leverage our prime London location to provide a holistic curriculum where pupils are exposed to a wide world of discovery, fostering independence, leadership, and a lifelong love of learning.
With over 70 clubs running each week, our extracurricular program is designed for breadth and balance. We pride ourselves on the quality of instruction; many of our clubs are led by external providers who are leading experts in their fields, ensuring your child receives professional-level coaching and mentorship right here at school.
Children can choose from a wide range of academic, languages, sport, performing arts and enrichment clubs, meaning there is something for every child.
Debating & Interview Club
Musical Theatre Company
Digital Creators Lab
Young Engineers LEGO
3D Design & Printing

Each year, we run ‘Key Skills Week’ in the Autumn Half Term. This is a dedicated focus on life skills, where pupils step away from traditional timetables to engage in immersive, skill-based learning that prepares them for future challenges.
Read about what our pupils got up to in the most recent Key Skills Week here…
We utilise our central London location to enrich the curriculum through frequent, carefully planned excursions. A glimpse into some of our recent excursions include…
As pupils progress, so do their adventures. From Year 3 upwards, we run annual residential trips. Our Seniors enjoy international cultural experiences in destinations such as Milan, Barcelona, and Amsterdam.
The KS Ski Tradition: A highlight of our calendar. We offer a Winter ski trip for all pupils from Year 4+, and a specialised Easter trip for our competitive team to participate in the IAPS championships.

Reception at Knightsbridge
The Reception year at Knightsbridge School is a milestone moment. It is the bridge between the discovery of the early years and the transition into the Junior School. As a leading London private school, our mission is to build the vital foundations of learning, ensuring every child transitions from a curious toddler into a confident, inquisitive pupil with a genuine love for school. Whether your child is moving up from our own Nursery or joining us for the very first time, we ensure the experience is smooth, supportive, and exciting.
Reception at a Glance
Classroom designed as a “Third Practitioner”; child-led discovery within a structured framework
Literacy, Mathematics, Understanding the World and Expressive Arts and Design
Specialist provision
Direct progression into Junior School (Year 1)
Sports at Holland Park and Burton Court
Arts performances including the Winter play
French and Spanish lessons
The Classroom as the ‘Third Practitioner’
Our Reception classrooms are not just rooms; they are designed as additional learning tools. Set up to be warm, nurturing, and stimulating, the layout acts as a “Third Practitioner”. Resources are positioned to encourage children to take the lead in their own education.
Child-Led Discovery: We foster independence by allowing children to pursue their own ideas and make choices, while our educators provide the framework to turn those choices into learning moments.
Specialist Integration: Children continue to enjoy our rich specialist timetable, enjoying sports in local green spaces such as Holland Park and Burton Court and building confidence in the Arts as they perform on stage in their Winter plays.
Learn more about the EYFS Curriculum here
A Personalised Learning Journey
We don’t believe in a “one size fits all” education. At Knightsbridge, we see your child as a unique individual with distinct skills, interests, and ideas, providing the high-quality, tailored attention expected of a top London private school.
Observation-Led Planning: We carefully observe each child’s spontaneous access to learning. These insights allow us to tailor day-to-day experiences to their specific well-being and developmental needs.
Digital Learning Journeys: We document this progress in a beautiful, personalised Learning Journey. Shared with parents at the end of each full term, this digital story captures their academic progress, social interactions, and amazing achievements that make the Reception year so special.
The Next Step
By the end of Reception, a KS student is more than just “school-ready.” They are independent thinkers who are comfortable and confident in their environment, have built strong academic foundations, and are eager to step into Year 1.
Learn more about the transition into our Junior school.
Make an enquiry for our Reception class at Knightsbridge School today.

Frequently Asked Questions About Reception
What curriculum does Reception follow at Knightsbridge School?
Reception follows our Early Years curriculum, built on the EYFS framework, with rich specialist provision in sport and the arts alongside core learning.
How is my child's progress tracked in Reception?
We use observation-led planning and document each child’s progress in a personalised digital Learning Journey, shared with parents at the end of every full term.
What happens after Reception at Knightsbridge?
Reception pupils progress directly into our Junior School (Year 1), continuing with the friends and teachers they already know.

Junior Performing Arts
At Knightsbridge School, we believe that the performing arts are a vital part of a holistic education. As a leading independent school in Knightsbridge, our creative curriculum is designed to inspire confidence, foster collaboration, and allow every pupil’s unique personality to shine.
We pride ourselves on an “all-rounder” ethos where every child is encouraged to ‘give it a go’. Whether your child is a budding lead actor or prefers the magic of technical production, there is a place for them to flourish. Our specialist teachers – many of whom have professional industry experience – guide pupils through a variety of disciplines including Music, Drama, and Dance.
Our Production Calendar
The performing arts calendar at KS is packed with opportunities for pupils to showcase their hard work and creativity:
The Year 4 Pantomime: A beloved highlight of the Autumn term, our Year 4 pupils bring festive cheer to the school with a high-energy performance before the Christmas break.
Junior Showcases: Pupils in Years 1-5 participate in annual Winter and Spring Showcases, building their performance stamina in a supportive environment.
The Summer Season: In the Summer term, our performance standards reach new heights with major productions. Recent hits include Mary Poppins and Shrek Junior.
The Chelsea Theatre Experience: To give our pupils a taste of the professional world, our Musical Theatre Company and Drama Company perform their summer shows at the renowned Chelsea Theatre. These audition-only groups allow pupils to work with full-scale sets, expert lighting, and bespoke costumes.
Our commitment to the arts extends beyond the stage. Through our performing arts programme pupils develop essential life skills:
Confidence & Wellbeing: Using the “KS Code,” we nurture resilient and happy performers.
Academic Innovation: We integrate modern technology into the arts, from music composition to digital set design.
Community Spirit: Whether it is the Interhouse Performing Arts Competition or the Show Choir performing at local landmarks like The Berkeley, our pupils remain deeply rooted in our local London community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Art & Drama | Knightsbridge Independent School
pageCache.text:
Senior Performing Arts
Building on from the foundations built in the Junior school, the Senior Performing Arts department continues with the ethos that every student has the talent and scope to achieve extraordinary things.
Performing Arts lessons take place weekly in the senior school timetable and students have the opportunity to develop core skills in Music, Drama and Dance. Senior students experience aspects of theatre production including filming, directing and producing scenes, choreographing their own dances and composing their own music scores. The curriculum is designed to expose students to a mature and extensive training programme that will equip them for study at GCSE level as well as prepare for potential scholarship applications and study in later life. It also harnesses essential skills in confidence, vocal projection and collaboration.
The senior school hosts a performance piece in the Spring Term that takes place in a professional theatre. Students audition for parts and work collaboratively with their peers to design bespoke sets, costume and lighting plots.
Music
Knightsbridge School is passionate about its musical offering. The Music curriculum from Nursery to GCSE level is designed to expose our students to a broad range of musical styles through singing, playing instruments, music technology, composing and listening and imparting a love of music. The curriculum is engaging and inclusive and will equip students with the skills to study at GCSE level or pursue a Music Scholarship if they wish.
Private tuition is offered to all pupils in the school on a broad range of instruments – brass, wind, strings, piano and keyboards, percussion, voice and drums. Music lessons are exceptionally popular and are scheduled on a rotational basis throughout the school. Children are encouraged to demonstrate their musical progress by performing in termly recitals and are entered into termly ABRSM examinations when they are ready.
Drama
The Drama curriculum is broad and varied and allows our children a space to grow in confidence on and off the stage. Our pupils, no matter their age, love taking on the roles of characters, discovering scripts, devising their own monologues, getting into costume and sharing incredible stories to an audience.
LAMDA and Trinity Drama examinations are popular at KS. Selected children are prepared and entered for these exams throughout the year and are very successful.
Dance
Dance at KS is very popular and is loved by the whole school community. In Dance, we have equal performance and technical focus. As part of the curriculum, we are developing the study of the IDTA syllabus and children will be entered for exams from across the school community.
Drama Company
We open auditions to all students in Y5-7 for a space in the Drama company. 15 exceptional actors get selected for their shown potential in acting and work together to produce a performance that takes place in the summer term at The Chelsea Theatre. Recent performances include A Twelfth Night and the incredibly successful A Midsummer Night’s Dream by our cast of 2022!
Students also work on the Trinity Drama Syllabus and prepare for potential Acting Scholarships at KS and other future school options.
This group annually prepares innovative pieces for ‘Poetry Together’. You can watch the most recent performances of ‘Skimbleshanks, the Railway Cat’ by T.S. Elliot and ‘The Crown’ by Carol Anne Duffy featuring two special guests from the Royal Hospital Chelsea here. In 2021 the Drama Company performed their bespoke performance of ‘The Queen’ in front of HRH Duchess of Cornwall.
Musical Theatre Company
We open auditions to all students in Y5-7 for a space in the Musical Theatre company. 15 students get selected for their shown potential in Musical Theatre including singing, dancing and acting. This group works to produce a group piece following the IDTA syllabus as well as their hit show which takes place in the summer term at the Chelsea Theatre.
Show Choir
Show choir is open to all students from Y4- Y11. pageCache.pageTitle: Prep School Knightsbridge & Chelsea | Knightsbridge School
pageCache.text:
A Leading Prep School in Knightsbridge & Chelsea
Behind our iconic blue doors on Pont Street, you’ll find a world of educational excellence with a real buzz – something we’ve coined the ‘KS Magic’.
But outside those doors, you will find world-famous department stores like Harrods, Harvey Nichols and Hermès. Or if shopping isn’t your thing, the Science, Natural History and V&A museums are also just a short walk away. Rather than stand intimidated by all these London landmarks, we consider ourselves among them as one of the few independent schools offering a truly seamless education journey – from Nursery all the way to GSCE.
Founded in 2006 by our founder, Magoo Giles, Knightsbridge School is a co-educational independent day school for children aged 3 to 16. Part of the Dukes Education family since 2018 and built on our own KS Code, we’ve provided exceptional eduactional service for 20 years to families in the Knightsbridge, Chelsea and Belgravia areas, offering a rare combination of excellence, community and happiness.
Book a Visit View Our Prospectus
Why Families Choose Knightsbridge School
Our excellent teaching is shaped by Six Aims:
Threaded through everything from Nursery to Year 11, our curriculum builds preparation for 11+ and 13+ entrance examinations follows the ISEB syllabus from Year 5, with senior staff tailoring the approach to each child rather than running a single fixed programme for every pupil.
Atmosphere
Autonomy
All-rounder
Attitude
Achievement
Wellbeing Woven Into the Week
Knightsbridge was one of the first schools to bring Place2Be, the children’s mental health charity, into daily school life. It sits alongside a values-led culture where staff know pupils individually, not just by year group.
A Track Record in the Arts, Not Just the Prospectus
Pupils here have performed in the West End, competed in fencing at Commonwealth Games level, and gone on to win senior school scholarships in music, drama and sport. One recent leaver was awarded an Honorary Fencing Scholarship at Harrow School, a fitting result for a school where the arts and sport are treated as seriously as anything in the classroom.
Small Enough to Know Every Child
Twenty years after admitting our first pupils in 2006, and twenty years into life in this postcode, Knightsbridge School remains genuinely close-knit: co-educational, non-selective at entry, and small enough that no child gets lost in the building around them.
A Prep School at the Heart of Knightsbridge & Chelsea
Distance from School
Knightsbridge Station (Piccadilly Line)
Sloane Square Station (Circle & District Line)

19, 22, 137, 452, C1 from Sloane Street
Given the density of the area, most local families walk, cycle or take a short bus journey rather than drive. For those who do need to park, the NCP car park at Cadogan Place and pay-and-display bays on surrounding streets are the closest options, though we’d always encourage walking where the school run allows.
A Strong Record, on Home Ground and Beyond
Recent Knightsbridge leavers have secured places and scholarships at schools including Queen’s College, JAGS, Alleyn’s, Francis Holland Sloane Square, Emanuel, Queen’s Gate, Dulwich College, Charterhouse, St Mary’s Ascot and Stowe, spanning academic, sporting, musical and dramatic achievement.
We are inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and are members of the Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS) and the Independent Schools Council (ISC). Our 2016 inspection recognised excellence across the board, and our most recent routine inspection took place in 2026. Full reports are available on our ISI Reports page.
One independent review described Knightsbridge as “a busy, happy school,” noting particular strength in the performing arts and imaginative use of its very urban site, a fair summary of a school that treats its central London setting as an asset rather than a constraint.
Frequently Asked Questions
What ages does Knightsbridge School accept?
Knightsbridge School is a co-educational day school for children aged 3 to 16, from Nursery through to Year 11 (GCSE), with a continuous path through Early Years, Juniors and Seniors.
Is Knightsbridge School close to Sloane Square and Chelsea?
Yes. The school is about 0.6 miles from Sloane Square station, with King’s Road and wider Chelsea a short walk away, and pupils regularly use nearby Chelsea sports grounds, including the Royal Hospital Chelsea, as part of school life.
Is Knightsbridge School a private school?
Yes. Knightsbridge School is an independent, fee-paying, non-selective school, inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and a member of IAPS and the ISC.
What areas do families travel from?
Most families live within walking distance in Knightsbridge, Belgravia and Chelsea, while others travel from South Kensington, Mayfair and further across central London via the Piccadilly, Circle and District lines.
Is Knightsbridge School suitable for international families?
Yes. Our central London location, close to embassies, international hotels and Heathrow links, makes us a natural choice for families relocating to London from overseas. Our International Families guide has further details on the application process.
Which senior schools do Knightsbridge pupils go on to?
Recent leavers have secured places and scholarships at schools including Queen’s College, JAGS, Alleyn’s, Emanuel, Dulwich College, Queen’s Gate, Charterhouse and St Mary’s Ascot.
How do I apply to Knightsbridge School?
The best first step is to book a place at an Open Morning or a weekly school tour, then complete our online registration form.

Junior Curriculum
In all subjects, teachers strive to spark imaginations, exploring ideas in new and unexpected ways. This is encouraged through asking big questions, developing pupils’ creative and critical thinking skills.
The Junior School’s varied curriculum inspires and equips our young learners. Science, History, Geography and RE are taught through termly topics in a stimulating and nurturing classroom environment. Opportunities are provided for our pupils to learn cooperatively, to develop respect for others and to become independent learners.
Specialist teachers instruct pupils in Languages, Art and Computing as well as in an extensive Performing Arts programme including Dance, Music and Drama. Each child takes part in a variety of sporting activities, ranging from swimming to netball and football.
As part of the curriculum for each class, teachers organise a variety of trips to places of interest during the course of each year. In the past, these have included art galleries and museums, Brighton, Tower of London, Kew Gardens, Barnes Wetland, Royal Courts of Justice and much more.
English
English
The English Department at Knightsbridge School operates a flexible curriculum that balances linguistic and literary work according to the children’s ability. In the Junior School (year 1-3), the emphasis is naturally upon technical accuracy and the acquisition of basic literacy skills.
Work is differentiated for all abilities, and the members of the Junior Team work closely with colleagues in the Learning Support Department. The English department seeks to develop pupils’ ability to communicate effectively in speech and writing, and to listen with understanding. We also seek to create enthusiastic, responsive and knowledgeable readers.
We see English as a subject that is skills based. As English teachers, we are enthusiastic about our subject, but ultimately we see our success in the creation of young people who are able to read and write with meaning, research, explore ideas, and question. With this in mind, pupils are exposed to a wide variety of prose, poetry and plays, and they engage with both fiction and non-fiction texts.
Every child comes to us with talents; we try to develop their creativity, broaden their knowledge and love of literature and help them say what they mean.
Mathematics
Mathematics
At KS, we employ a child-centred approach to teaching Mathematics, as we know the learning requirements for each pupil is different from one pupil to another. We combine the more conventional and traditional teaching methods with the new ideas adapted from the Government’s National Strategies. Every effort is made to help the children realise that the subject is a lot of fun where games and practical activities encourage pupils to use imagination and initiative.
It is not just about working through exercises in a book. We believe this provides a more stimulating environment and provides the children with a more relevant outlook in their understanding of other curriculum areas and the outside world. Mathematics is taught by the class teachers in mixed ability groups.
Where possible we will use as many practical activities to explore and explain the topics. The main focus in these formative years is to develop their confidence in using numbers. This will be introduced as recognition, sequencing and then starting to use the four operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division). Other areas such as shape, space and measures,
Handling data and basic properties of numbers will be included in this introduction and, as we work on a spiral curriculum, each topic area will be covered in more depth in its following cycle. Mental arithmetic games play a large part in the pupils’s learning as this is vital to build self-confidence. We also focus on the acquisition of times tables to aid mental arithmetic.
Science
Science
The Science Department at Knightsbridge works to inspire children’s curiosity and enthusiasm about science, fostering critical thinking and enquiry skills. We carefully sequence learning to lay the foundations for children to understand the world around them, and to strive to ask, explore, and answer scientific questions.
We want children to not only understand the theory of science but to gain knowledge of the uses and implications of science, today and for the future. We build careers and diversity into the program, so that all students can build a nuanced and personalised understanding of the development of this field, as well as their place and potential within it.
Children use practical examples, models and experiences to build an understanding of scientific concepts and are supported and encouraged to test their ideas in increasingly refined ways. Upon entering senior classes, we hope for all students to be confident and eloquent scientists, who can independently select and design different forms of inquiry to answer their own questions.
Humanities
Humanities
The Humanities play a central role in our broad and balanced curriculum. Pupils learn History and Geography from year 1-6 with Classical Civilisations introduced from year 5. Building a strong understanding of the world in which is live, empowered by historical, geographical, and cultural awareness is one of key aims in Humanities. Our Perspectives course teaches philosophy, religion and ethics and encourages students to become curious and critical thinkers, empowered to engage with current affairs.
Phonics & Reading
Phonics & Reading
Phonics underpins all Reading and Writing in the Juniors and children in Year 1 are taught a synthetic phonic programme using Read, Write Inc. In this programme, children learn the 44 common sounds of the English language. Once children know these sounds, they are able to learn how to sound-blend words for reading, develop comprehension skills, improve handwriting skills and spelling and write about their reading. Children are grouped across the year group, to ensure that instruction is closely matched to their needs. Children progress quickly through the scheme and graduate into a closely tailored English programme.
We expect the majority of our children to reach this point by the end of year 1. The reading skills that children acquire early on are continually developed throughout their time at school. As role models, teachers share their passion for reading and model the skills to strengthen and support children’s reading development. This is consistent across all subjects so that children learn that reading forms the basis of so much of their education. Children will read independently in school, as well as with an adult, and this should then be continued at home so that children are practising their reading skills. Children will bring home levelled books to share at home, and comprehension and understanding skills can therefore be further developed.
Art
Art
Art at Knightsbridge School is taught by a specialist teacher in the Juniors. Children use the well-equipped studio right at the top of the school, allowing for a spacious working area, which is full of light. This offers an environment that is both a creative and stimulating place to work. All the children enjoy a double lesson of Art per week.
In the Juniors we also encourage children to do art activities in the classroom to link to their Inquiry topic. The main objective of the Art department is for the children to develop a love of creating. The children learn and enjoy all aspects of the process from the initial sketches to finished pieces. We aim to provide a safe environment, which encourages the children to express themselves in their own unique way regardless of attainment level.
Children are introduced to a diverse range of artists, movements and culture. They are exposed to a wide variety of materials, mediums and processes: drawing, painting, textiles, perspective, sculpture, ceramics, batik, printmaking, collage; in order to give every child the opportunity to discover their own potential. Large-scale projects and individual works are displayed proudly around the school and where appropriate entered into competitions and external exhibitions.
Computing
Computing
Computing at Knightsbridge School is an exciting, diverse and creative subject. Emphasis is placed on teaching transferable skills that enable students to use ICT both as a tool to produce well-presented work and to communicate ideas effectively. Making sure that forthcoming generations are up-to-date with new technology is always a challenge.
Students at KS will be exposed to the latest software and hardware so that they will be equipped to deal with the ever-changing nature of the technological 21st Century. In year 1 and year 2 pupils are taught ICT skills through their Humanities lessons by the pupil’s teacher on either laptops or their class Chrome books. In Year 3 pupils have a specific Computing lesson which is taught by a specialist teacher in the ICT suite. ICT is extensively used in all other lessons in order to enhance the learning experience of other subjects.
In the Juniors, classrooms have banks of brand new Chromebooks to allow pupils to explore ICT at various times throughout the day. All classrooms are equipped with interactive whiteboards and each teacher has an iPad to further enhance learning and capture films and photographs.
Languages
Languages
All pupils study a language, choosing from either French or Spanish. Each pupil continues with the same language from year 1-3 to in order to best develop their reading, speaking and listening skills. In year 4 the options broaden, and pupils can either continue with the same language or pick up Italian or Mandarin instead. Pupils learn languages through stories, games, role play, rhymes and songs. Emphasis is put on spoken language.
